title: Complaint of RE Mark A. Grasso et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed Philadelphia Presbytery’s approval of Jason Hsu’s ordination examination.
first_summary: Ruling on a challenge to Presbytery’s approval of a candidate who believed women could hold the office of deacon but promised not to ordain them, the SJC denied the complaint and affirmed Presbytery. It distinguished subscription to doctrinal standards from approval of BCO practices and deferred to Presbytery’s judgment that the candidate could credibly take the third ordination vow.
summary: The complaint challenged Presbytery’s approval of a candidate who believed women could hold the diaconal office but promised to follow the BCO, which permits only men to be ordained as deacons. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed approval of his ordination examination. It held that a BCO difference is evaluated through compliance, doctrinal, and ordination-vow inquiries; the record supported compliance and a credible vow, while complainants had not identified violated doctrinal standards. Absent contrary evidence, Presbytery’s judgment received deference.

sources.supports: Identity of complaint 2008-10, ordination issue, three-part inquiry, application, denial, and affirmance.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Lines 75–80 identify Grasso et al.’s complaint as SJC 2008-10; lines 224–230 give the majority’s operative disposition and vote.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 90–94 frame whether Presbytery erred by approving for ordination a candidate with a stated BCO difference concerning women and the diaconal office.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 98–99 answer no; lines 147–175 state the three-part inquiry; lines 185–228 apply deference, note the unarticulated doctrinal claim, and deny the complaint while affirming Presbytery.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Lines 226–228 reaffirm that the BCO permits only men to be ordained as deacons. Lines 234–350 are separate concurrence and dissent, not adopted majority reasoning.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision is incorporated by reference; the 1984 case mentioned at lines 49–51 appears only in Presbytery’s committee report.

source_limits: The majority opinion jointly resolves 2008-01 and 2008-10. This synopsis isolates 2008-10’s challenge to ordination; the licensure ruling belongs to companion case 2008-01.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the challenged approval and the candidate’s stated difference.
score_reasons.decision: States both denial of the complaint and affirmance of Presbytery’s action.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains the adopted three-part inquiry, record findings, pleading deficiency, and deference.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the distinction between BCO compliance and doctrinal subscription without weakening the male-only ordination rule.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates the majority holding from the joint licensure issue and separate opinions.
score_reasons.economy: All details explain the dispute, governing inquiry, or result.
